reviews.review:
I'll start by saying I found the price of this game to be pretty insulting. It doesn't reflect where this game sits in the broader indie horror game market. One could argue that it's worth a bit more since there are multiple endings, but the endings don't really feel like true meaningful endings. It's like there is the full game plus a few ways to end the game early. 
I really wish I could recommend this game though, because there are definitely parts of it I really enjoyed. I found it to be quite a bit scarier than I was expecting. Even though the antagonist was a fairly common store-bought asset, it was used to great effect. The sound design of the game was also pretty great. But I have to weigh the things I really liked against the fact that I played through this game multiple times and encountered game-breaking bugs nearly every time. I don't think it's impossible to get through it without encountering bugs, but they're there and shouldn't be. Among the bugs was- once the inventory menu stayed stuck on the screen no matter what. That's an issue I've ran into with a few games that were made with Horror Engine. Another time my framerate dropped down to single digits and just stayed that way, no matter what settings I changed. I went all the way down to 1080p LOW and it persisted. Couple the bugs with the game not having any save feature, and it's a real headache. 
In summary, I feel like this game maintains the same theme that has been too common lately, close to being recommendable, but ultimately falling short. Considering the gameplay on its own, I would recommend it, but considering the game as a whole with it's price tag and the bugs, I just can't recommend. https://youtu.be/ggqlaXJQMmI?si=zx1IrApuq-ohoxI-
